## TL;DR

The Releases page no longer blames an unrelated workflow. The release-failure banner now reads only the latest run of the configured `release.workflow` file (`release.yml`) for the viewed tag, and a lagging Homebrew row reads **Updating** while the tap's own run is active or within five minutes of a successful release run. Most of the code and tests were already on the branch from earlier WIP checkpoints; this session confirmed them against the acceptance criteria, fixed one styling bug in the new `updating` state, and ran the checks.

## Work and rationale

The cause in the task was `fetchCiFailure` listing every push-triggered run for the tag and reporting the first failure. The branch replaces that with `inspectReleaseWorkflow` in `src/server/distribution.ts`. It calls `actions/workflows/<basename>/runs?branch=<tag>&event=push&per_page=5`, where the basename comes from `releaseWorkflowBasename(config.release.workflow)`. Only that workflow's newest run can produce `ciFailure`. If the newest run succeeded, its `updated_at` becomes `releaseSucceededAt`, which drives the grace window. If `release.workflow` is unset, no CI context is fetched at all, so no banner can appear.

For failed runs, `failedStepForRun` reads the run's jobs and reports the first step with `conclusion: "failure"`, which is what the banner quotes.

For criterion 3, `applyHomebrewUpdatingState` changes a Homebrew row from `out-of-sync` to `updating` in two cases. The first is that the tap repository has a run in `in_progress`, `queued`, `waiting`, `requested` or `pending`, checked through `homebrewTapUpdateInProgress`. The second is that `releaseSucceededAt` is less than `DISTRIBUTION_HOMEBREW_GRACE_MS` (five minutes) old. Otherwise the row stays `out-of-sync`. The tap check only runs for rows that are already out of sync, so healthy channels cost no extra requests.

On the UI side, `ReleasesView.vue` gains an `updating` channel state with the label "Updating" and an aggregate "Distribution destinations are updating" line when every non-matching row is updating. `docs/releases.md` now says the banner refers only to the configured `release.workflow` file and that unrelated workflows never produce it, and it describes the Updating state and its grace window. `repoos.toml` is untouched.

I chose to key the grace window on the release run's `updated_at` rather than on when RepoOS first noticed the tag. That is the moment the workflow finished, so it matches what the user is waiting on. The window is a named constant so the tests can pin it.

## Approaches tried

The first option considered was filtering the all-runs list by `workflow_path` or name. I preferred the per-workflow endpoint because it returns only the release workflow's runs and needs no client-side filtering. The per-workflow endpoint takes the file basename, so `releaseWorkflowBasename` strips any directory prefix from `.github/workflows/release.yml`.

For the grace window I considered a fixed timestamp from the RepoOS release record. I rejected it because the release record may not carry the workflow finish time, and the GitHub run's `updated_at` is already available from the call that determines failure.

## Challenges and blockers

This session started from an existing branch state, so part of my work was verification rather than new implementation. Comparing against the merge-base showed that the branch diff is four files: `docs/releases.md`, `src/server/distribution.ts`, `src/ui-app/src/views/ReleasesView.vue` and `src/ui-app/tests/distribution.test.ts`. The other `work/` files that looked like drift in `git diff main` came from main moving ahead, not from this branch.

I found a real styling bug in the new `updating` rule. It used `--cyan-tint` and `--cyan-border-tint`, and neither token is declared in `style.css` for any theme, so the badge would have rendered with no background. The existing cyan references elsewhere in the file share the same gap, which I did not change. I switched the new rule to `--violet`, `--violet-tint` and `--violet-border-tint`, which are declared in the themes. The tint appears in 15 of 16 theme blocks, so one theme may fall back to its default.

Two test files failed under bare `bunx vitest` because the Vue plugin is not loaded there. The repo's `bun run test` wrapper loads them correctly, and the fault was in how I invoked the runner, not in the code.

I did not verify against live GitHub. The network is unavailable in this sandbox, so the tests use mocked responses for the workflow runs, jobs and tap runs. The real Adoption matrix and release workflow shapes are inferred from the task description.

## Key learnings

Scoping an Actions query to one workflow file is much cleaner than filtering a repository-wide run list, and it removes a whole class of misattribution. The per-workflow endpoint takes the basename of the workflow path, so a config that stores the full `.github/workflows/...` path needs to be normalized first.

A "pending" state needs its own signal. Treating a lagging downstream row as failed made every Homebrew propagation look like a broken release. Grounding "updating" in observable facts, a tap run in progress or a release that just succeeded, lets the page stay honest without guessing.

Tokens used in new CSS should be checked against the theme declarations, not assumed to exist because other rules reference them. An undeclared token fails silently.

## Verification

`REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed: staleness, format, lint, build, CSS layers, theme and hard-coded color guards, rendered contrast audit, bare-require guard and the UI smoke test. Its test step was skipped because this environment hands tests to the remote runner. Locally, `bun run test` over `distribution.test.ts`, `releases-distribution-view.test.ts`, `release-cut-next.test.ts` and `boot-timing.test.ts` passed 80 of 80. The distribution suite includes the four #1090 cases: unrelated failed run with a successful release run gives no banner, a failed release run gives a banner naming the failed step, a lagging Homebrew row in the grace window reads Updating, and the same row after the window reads out of sync when the tap is idle.

No preview was requested, and no live API outcome was observed.
